nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration / third-party payment gateway fees setup
Cloud infrastructure (staging + prod) during build phase
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / consulting
Contingency / misc tooling licenses (design, testing tools)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is based on backlog point sizing and standard delivery ratios, not observed velocity.
1 story point translates to roughly 6-7 hours of blended effort across roles, adjusted per task type (integration/migration tasks weighted higher).
Team capacity: 1.5 FTE Backend, 1.0 FTE Frontend, 0.6 FTE QA, 0.4 FTE DevOps, assumed available for the ~4-5 month duration implied by the 1250 backend hours (approx 208 hrs/month per FTE).

DevOps Engineer is staffed thinly (0.4 FTE) relative to the CI/staging, observability and legacy decommission work required; hours were kept proportionate to capacity and this role may become a schedule bottleneck.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) hours are concentrated on Urgent/High priority items (auth, payments, RBAC, GDPR) with lighter coverage on Low priority items; full regression coverage of all 24 items at this staffing level is optimistic.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumed to require external tooling/consulting spend in addition to Backend hours, given the volume (400k records / 2M invoice lines).
Non-labour costs cover cloud infra during build, Stripe integration setup fees, migration tooling, and a general contingency for licenses/tools.

Scenario spread (Optimistic/Most Likely/High) reflects uncertainty mainly in the migration (PW-8), payment integration (PW-7), and multi-currency (PW-14) tasks, which have the highest estimation risk.
Priority breakdown allocates each labour/non-labour line proportionally to the backlog points of tasks in that priority band.
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 24 tasks / ~205 story points. Hours were allocated per task using a blended ~6-7 hrs/point baseline, weighted up for integration-heavy or data-migration tasks (PW-7 Payment, PW-8 Migration, PW-14 Multi-currency) and weighted down for lower-complexity or admin-style tasks (PW-12, PW-23, PW-24). Backend Developer absorbs the largest share due to API, RBAC, payment, migration and search work; Frontend Developer covers the design system, dashboard, invoice UI, accessibility and responsive work; QA Engineer time is concentrated on urgent/high-risk flows (auth, payments, RBAC, GDPR) with lighter pass on low-priority items; DevOps Engineer covers CI/staging setup (PW-1), observability (PW-22) and decommission (PW-24), but at 0.4 FTE this is the tightest-staffed role relative to demand. Non-labour costs cover cloud infrastructure during the build phase, Stripe integration fees, external migration tooling/consulting for the Oracle migration, and a contingency line for design/testing tool licenses. Total labour + non-labour comes to $259,012.50 (Most Likely / P50). Optimistic (P10, $222,000) assumes migration and payment integration go smoothly with fewer webhook/reconciliation edge cases and no major legacy schema surprises. High (P90, $300,000) reflects the risk that legacy migration, multi-currency settlement, and Stripe reconciliation each require additional rework cycles, plus possible QA bottleneck given the thin 0.6 FTE staffing. No historical actuals exist for this project, so all effort ratios are based on backlog sizing heuristics rather than observed velocity, which is flagged as a key assumption/risk.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 points) to a later phase; support agents can use direct DB/read-only tooling in the interim.
reductions.effect: Removes an estimated 130 hours of combined Backend/Frontend/QA effort from this phase.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting, Low priority, 8 points) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API, Low priority, 5 points) to a post-launch backlog.
reductions.effect: Removes roughly 100 hours of Backend/Frontend/QA effort tied to two low-priority, non-blocking items.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) scope for launch to USD + EUR only, adding PLN in a later release.
reductions.effect: Cuts an estimated 70 hours of Backend/QA effort spent on the third-currency FX handling and settlement edge cases.

reductions.description: Use a managed migration service or Stripe-hosted reconciliation reporting instead of fully custom tooling for PW-8, reducing external consulting spend.
reductions.effect: Lowers the non-labour 'Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/consulting' line from $8,000 to $5,000.

reductions.description: Combine PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) with routine DevOps maintenance work rather than dedicated sprint time, given DevOps is the most capacity-constrained role.
reductions.effect: Removes an estimated 40 hours of dedicated DevOps Engineer time from this phase.
